title: Jobs
description: Wire shapes of the job routes: the worker's internal routes and the signed-in user's public routes (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md sections 6 and 8). Each message is a definition under $defs.

HeartbeatAction.description: What the worker should do next: carry on, or end the job because the user cancelled it or it reached its stop limit.

Transfer.description: One file a job reads or writes (ADR-005). Locally the url points at the API's /internal/jobs/{id}/files route and needs the worker token; in the cloud it is a presigned storage URL.

name.description: The file's name within the job, for example model.step.

params.description: Job-type specific parameters, for example an ImportParams (geometry.schema.json); null when the type has none.

WorkerSoftware.description: Versions of the worker that claims a job (ADR-032), recorded on the job so a run can state what produced it. Null where the worker lacks the program.

clearfea.description: The worker package's version, with the source commit it was built from after a + when known, for example 0.0.0+d9d394b.

machineSize.description: The machine size the worker runs on (M10.6, ADR-099), from CLEARFEA_MACHINE_SIZE: it is given only that size's jobs, and the default size's also takes the jobs that have no size (import, report). Left out by a local worker, which takes every size's jobs.

ClaimResponse.description: Answer to a claim when a job was claimed (HTTP 200). No job to claim is HTTP 204 with no body.

log.description: Log text the job wrote since the previous heartbeat, appended to the job's log as one chunk (ADR-030).

HostCheckIn.description: Body of POST /internal/hosts/check-in (M12.4, ADR-120): the solver host's compute manager says it is up, at start and every intervalSeconds whatever its lanes are doing. With MACHINES=vps the API refuses new jobs while no host has checked in for 120 s.

host.description: The host's name, as the admin page shows it.

HostLoad.description: The solver host's load when it checked in (M12.3, ADR-109, ADR-123), kept as host_stats for 14 days. CPU and steal are shares of all the host's CPU time since the previous check-in, from 0 to 1, absent at the manager's first check-in; memory and disk in bytes.

steal.description: CPU time the hypervisor gave to other machines while this one wanted it.

diskTotalBytes.description: Of the file system holding Docker's data, where the jobs' scratch volumes are.

containers.description: Containers running on the host, job containers and others.

ContainerStats.description: Body of POST /internal/jobs/{id}/stats (M12.3, ADR-109, ADR-123): what the compute manager measured of one try of a job from its container, sent once the container has ended. Memory, CPU and disk come from Docker's container statistics sampled every 5 s, so a peak shorter than that can be missed. The API answers 204, or 404 when the worker has no try of that job still without these statistics.

image.description: The id of the worker image the container ran (sha256:...).

exitCode.description: The container's exit code; above 128 it was ended by signal exitCode - 128. Null when it never started.

outOfMemory.description: Docker stopped the container at its memory limit.

runMs.description: From the container's start to its end.

samples.description: Statistics samples taken; with none, memory, CPU and disk are left out.

cpuSeconds.description: CPU time the container used over all its CPUs, at the last sample.

cpuPeak.description: The most CPUs busy between two samples (6 is six CPUs busy).

diskWrittenBytes.description: Bytes the container wrote to block devices, its scratch volume among them, at the last sample.

intervalSeconds.description: Seconds until the next check-in is due.

Metering.description: What the worker measured of a job (ADR-033): billableMs is the wall-clock time from the start to the end of the job's handler on the machine, in whole milliseconds. Queue time and the worker's start-up are outside it. Sent for every job; the API charges only metered job types.

result.description: Job-type specific summary, stored as given.

failureMessage.description: What went wrong and what to do about it, in plain language for the job's owner.

CompleteStopped.description: The worker ended the job because a heartbeat told it to (cancel or stop, M8.2): it reports the time it used. The API records the job as cancelled or stopped at its limit, as it asked, and charges the time (DECISIONS "Failed runs").

CreateJobRequest.description: Body of POST /api/jobs. Only a noop job is queued directly; later job types are created by the routes for the records they work on.

JobView.description: A job as its owner sees it. Timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC strings.

JobListResponse.description: Answer to GET /api/jobs: the signed-in user's most recent jobs, newest first.

JobWait.description: How a job that has not finished is getting on (M11.2, ADR-112). Sent as `wait` with the answers the screens poll while a job works on what they show: GET /api/jobs/{id}, /api/geometries/{id}, /api/simulations/{id}/mesh, /api/runs/{id} and /api/runs/{id}/report. Left out once the job has finished.

queuePosition.description: While the job is queued, its place among the queued jobs of its machine size, counting every user's jobs: 1 is next. Null once a worker has claimed it.

machineStarting.description: True on the live site while the job is queued and no machine of its size is running, or one is being started (ADR-103). Always false locally, where the worker is always there.

retryAfter.description: Seconds after which asking again is worth it. The browser waits at least this long, and never more than 30 s.

ErrorResponse.description: Body of any 4xx or 5xx answer: what is wrong and what to do about it.
